subject: problem with joint model of BYM and SPDE

messages.author: 512954c24bf42874
messages.subject: problem with joint model of BYM and SPDE
parts:
Hi all，
I am new to INLA.

I used incidence data (provincial level) to build the BYM mode.

And I used the point-referenced data to build spatial model in the same region.

I want to joint the two models by sharing the same spatial effect use other methods to joint this two model.  Is there any possible for INLA package to reach this? The ‘copy model’ seems only work in the model built by SPDE.

Detail code in the appendix.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problem with joint model of BYM and SPDE
parts:
Hi,

One spatial effect is defined at the mesh nodes while the other is defined at the areal id. In order to share one of them in the linear predictor where the other is primarily used, you need to do some "projection" into the other "model domain". Both will have to use the 'copy' feature in INLA. Either you have to "collect" the areal level effect for point referred observation or to project the continuous domain effect from the mesh nodes into the areal level. There are technical implication details and assumptions at the linear predictor level for the latter. Thus *one way* would be to copy the bym model to the linear predictor for the point referred data model. All you need is to create an index for each data location identifying which area it belongs to and use it as f(id.point.area, copy='area', ...) where 'area' is the name of the index for the bym model. In order to implement it in plain inla you may have to use inla.stack() for the areal data and merge both data stacks. This would be easier using inlabru.

best regards,
Elias
